scope: CARET-PLAN.md section 10 item 40 closure: one repackaged app whose check:packaged run is green, plus the durable fix for the dev shell's LaunchServices identity.
command: cd desktop && npx gulp vscode-darwin-arm64-min ; CARET_HOST_NODE=~/.caret-tools/node-v24.18.0-darwin-arm64/bin/node bun run package:mac ; bun run check:packaged

checkPackaged.result: OK   packaged Caret.app matches the current patch set
checkPackaged.freshness: both shell bundles are at or after the newest patch; the gulp rebuild rewrote them at 09:29-09:32, after every patch file

devShellIdentity.problem: `gulp electron` writes desktop/.build/electron/Caret.app, and desktop/scripts/code.sh launches it. The packaging task and the dev shell both read the same build/lib/electron.ts config, so both shipped com.caret.editor. LaunchServices keys an app by that identifier, so `open -a Caret`, Finder, and any re-registration pass could resolve to the incomplete dev shell -- no app payload and none of the Caret surfaces -- instead of VSCode-darwin-arm64/Caret.app.
devShellIdentity.firstAttemptRejected: Adding the dev identifier to build/lib/electron.ts gave the packaged app the same com.caret.editor.dev, because gulp's package task spreads that config: the packaged bundle's Info.plist was byte-identical to the dev one. Reverted before it could ship.
devShellIdentity.secondAttemptRejected: Separating only the identifier, then also renaming the shell to 'Caret (Dev)', still left two Caret bundles on disk. The user asked for one build; caught on review.
devShellIdentity.fix: scripts/lib/app-icon.ts#removeDevBundle unregisters the dev shell with lsregister -u and deletes it. scripts/build-caret.ts calls it in the --desktop block. A desktop build now leaves exactly one Caret: VSCode-darwin-arm64/Caret.app. The dev shell is recreated on demand by desktop/scripts/code.sh, so the dev window still works when wanted.
devShellIdentity.guard: The shell and the packaged app can share com.caret.editor, so removal is guarded by two properties a mis-resolved path cannot satisfy: the bundle must sit under the desktop/.build tree, and it must lack Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js, the payload only a real Caret has.

verified.buildLeavesOneCaret: node build/lib/electron.ts recreates the shell (id com.caret.editor), then `bun scripts/build-caret.ts --desktop` removes it: `test -d desktop/.build/electron/Caret.app` is false afterwards, while VSCode-darwin-arm64/Caret.app stays com.caret.editor.
verified.guardRefusesPackage: removeDevBundle('/Users/pond/caret/VSCode-darwin-arm64/Caret.app') -> false, still exists; removeDevBundle(dev shell path) -> true, removed.
verified.launchServices: lsregister -dump lists one Caret entry: /Users/pond/caret/VSCode-darwin-arm64/Caret.app -> name 'Caret', id com.caret.editor.
verified.runningApp: The window open at the end of this session is /Users/pond/caret/VSCode-darwin-arm64/Caret.app/Contents/MacOS/Caret (the packaged build that passed check:packaged); the dev shell was never launched.

notCovered: Running desktop/scripts/code.sh recreates the dev shell and re-registers it as a second Caret while that dev session is alive. That is the dev launcher doing what it is for; a plain `--desktop` build no longer leaves one behind.
The dev shell and the packaged app share the data folder (~/.caret), because desktop/argv.json is written from product.json alone. Only relevant while code.sh runs the dev window; not addressed.
